__.lastyy.__: Bastian "Bones" Lastyy arrived with the evening ration party, carrying a lucky button and a borrowed coat two sizes too big.
Blackwater Canal is in Hegemony hands. Bastian "Bones" Lastyy stopped arguing about the next watch and went to check the stores.
_hunter_warren_: Wendel "Shadow" Warren came up with a draft of replacements on Day 6. Nobody asked his name until the third night. After that, everyone knew it.
Wendel "Shadow" Warren wrote a letter for Karel Mccauley's mother, because Karel could not find the words. Karel signed it.
Wendel "Shadow" Warren pulled Matthias Fxx out of a flooded shell hole at Lantern Hill. Neither has mentioned it since. Both remember.

Wendel "Shadow" Warren found a shirt button in the bread. He ate around it and kept the button. Both were useful. A letter from home found Wendel "Shadow" Warren before the night shift. Wendel "Shadow" Warren folded it small and kept it close.

A football came over the parapet from the Concord side with Leopold "Brick" Moovin's name scratched on it. Wendel "Shadow" Warren kicked it back. It did not come again. A letter from home found Wendel "Shadow" Warren before the night shift. Wendel "Shadow" Warren folded it small and kept it close.

Day 10. The Hegemony took Blackwater Canal. From the heights Wendel "Shadow" Warren could see the whole Concord line, and for the first time the war looked winnable. A letter from home found Wendel "Shadow" Warren before the night shift. Wendel "Shadow" Warren folded it small and kept it close.
caden.w26: Quentin Caden came up the line in the rain with a rosary of rough beads and nothing else. The sergeant wrote him down as Private and pointed at the mud. News that the Concord had taken Verdel Ridge reached Quentin Caden during supper. The same stew suddenly tasted better.
Quentin Caden made a list of things to buy on leave. It started with socks and ended with a meal nobody could call a ration.
Rumour reached S-F6 that the war would be over by spring. Quentin Caden has heard it before. So has everyone.

Quentin Caden got a letter from Clara. Two pages, one of them only about the weather back home. He read that page most. Day 6. Hill 304 fell to the Hegemony. Quentin Caden watched their flag go up on the heights and dug his trench a little deeper.
A man asked Quentin Caden to describe Coldwater without mentioning the weather. He began with the steepest street and ended with the cheapest lunch.
Quentin Caden wrote back to Clara and tore it up three times. The fourth version says almost nothing, which is how he knows it is the right one.
Quentin Caden of the Concord and Edmund Ringwraith of the Hegemony share the same habit: a whistle at midnight. Both lines at Calvary Farm now wait for it before they sleep.
No post for Quentin Caden this week. He checks the sack anyway, every day, and pretends he was only looking for tobacco.
The Hegemony won Blackwater Canal. In S-F6, Quentin Caden listened to three explanations and trusted none of them.
hogggogins: Isidor "Spark" Hogggogins came up the line with a bullet that missed him and nothing else. The sergeant wrote him down as Private and pointed at the mud.
jak_11.7: In Belmonte, Hugo Jak was a schoolteacher. In P-F10, he is a number and a rifle. He has told everyone he intends to be a schoolteacher again.
jules95s: Day 9. The corporal put Quentin "Brick" Jules beside a veteran and said to copy everything except the language.
Blackwater Canal is in Hegemony hands. Quentin "Brick" Jules stopped arguing about the next watch and went to check the stores.
mrbojo1992: Bastian Mrbojo arrived on Day 9 and found the section asleep. The welcome had to wait until somebody needed the kettle.

The gun at R-C2 jammed twice and fired once. Once was enough: Konrad Embersky, badly wounded. The Hegemony won Blackwater Canal. In R-C2, Bastian Mrbojo listened to three explanations and trusted none of them.
paraop96: Rafael Paraop introduced himself as a brewer from Ashford Vale. The corporal repeated the name correctly. That helped more than the advice.
The report confirmed that the Hegemony held Blackwater Canal. Rafael Paraop read the last line twice, looking for something the first reading had missed.
rossfm82: On the way to S-S6, Leopold Rossfm tried to memorise every turn. By the dugout door, he was simply glad someone else knew the way. After what happened at Sorrow Copse, Leopold Rossfm asked to serve as a sniper. Nobody argued.

Leopold Rossfm lay in the ruins of Lantern Hill from dawn to dusk. He did not fire once. That is also a kind of victory. A letter from home found Leopold Rossfm before the night shift. Leopold Rossfm folded it small and kept it close.
Leopold Rossfm noticed a loophole that had been dark for days. He watched it until dusk and wrote down what changed.
Asked what he wanted after the war, Leopold Rossfm said a chair. After some thought: a chair nobody else was sitting on.

A bullet went through Leopold Rossfm's upper arm at S-S6 and broke the bone. He held the arm across his chest and walked half the way back before his legs gave out. Shot by Otto "Parson" Vicious of the Hegemony (@darth._.vicious). Leopold Rossfm was killed outright at S-S6, a single bullet from across the wire. Shot by Otto "Parson" Vicious of the Hegemony (@darth._.vicious).
Henrik Rossfm had heard about Leopold Rossfm's courage. At S-S6, he also heard about the snoring, the cards and the terrible handwriting.
sedlomancz: Henrik Sedlomancz reported to R-F14 with a pocket Bible with a hole in it sewn into his tunic lining. The sergeant pretended not to notice.
Henrik Sedlomancz's First Wave ribbon drew a question at supper. He remembered the queue at the depot more clearly than the speech.
Henrik Sedlomancz left the work of a rifleman to become a runner. Someone from the old section came over to see how it was going.

The company barber offered a choice of styles. Henrik Sedlomancz asked to see the second one. The barber laughed. The Concord hold Verdel Ridge now, and they can see straight into R-F14. Henrik Sedlomancz has learned to walk bent double.
A scrap of newspaper advertised a sale of garden furniture. Henrik Sedlomancz worked out how many months of pay a comfortable afternoon would cost.

A bucket appeared above the Concord parapet at Lantern Hill. Henrik Sedlomancz fired. Emil "Shadow" Knightowlvt pulled the bucket down. Later a sign went up: 'Water costs enough already.' A letter from home found Henrik Sedlomancz before the night shift. Henrik Sedlomancz folded it small and kept it close.

Wendel "Mole" Freddie lent Henrik Sedlomancz a pencil. It came back wrapped in a scrap of paper that said 'One good turn'. On Day 6, Hill 304 passed to the Hegemony. Henrik Sedlomancz wrote the name in his diary with unusual care.

Henrik Sedlomancz dreamt about missing a train. Waking up here felt like a harsh punishment for it. A letter from home found Henrik Sedlomancz before the night shift. Henrik Sedlomancz folded it small and kept it close.

Henrik Sedlomancz measured the remaining pencil against the remaining paper. For once, the supplies seemed likely to run out together. A letter from home found Henrik Sedlomancz before the night shift. Henrik Sedlomancz folded it small and kept it close.
A bullet bounced off the trench wall and caught Henrik Sedlomancz across the shin at R-F14. It bled a lot and meant very little. Shot by Gideon Actioncam of the Concord (@actioncam3000).

A bullet struck Henrik Sedlomancz below the ribs at R-F14. He kept asking whether the post was still manned until the bearers took him away. Shot by Florian "Doc" Guyy of the Concord (@proto_guyy). A letter from home found Henrik Sedlomancz before the night shift. Henrik Sedlomancz folded it small and kept it close.
There was no room for Henrik Sedlomancz. He died in the night under a borrowed coat, a few yards from a bed that never came free.

Another member of the House of Sedlomancz reached the line: Ivo Sedlomancz. He asked where Henrik Sedlomancz had slept, then chose a different corner. Number 57 on the early rolls: Ivo Sedlomancz. The First Wave ribbon arrived with instructions about where to sew it and no needle.
